name: Entity Blueprint
description: Bidirectional JSON entity serialization for AI workflows.

suggests.drupal/ai: Required by the entity_blueprint_ai submodule for AI agent tool integration.
suggests.drush/drush: Provides Drush commands for serialization, deserialization, and schema generation.

project_description: Entity Blueprint provides a clean JSON interface for Drupal entities aimed at AI and external-system workflows: serialize any fieldable entity (including Layout Builder pages with nested paragraphs, inline blocks, and opaque third-party settings) to a simplified JSON format, modify the JSON, then deserialize it back into a valid, unsaved Drupal entity with two-phase validation and structured error feedback. The base module is a standalone data/abstraction layer with no runtime dependency beyond Drupal core. Optional experimental submodules add AI function-call tooling (entity_blueprint_ai, entity_blueprint_config_ai), config-entity support (entity_blueprint_config), Anthropic/Claude skill formatting (entity_blueprint_ai_anthropic), and prompt-capture developer diagnostics (entity_blueprint_ai_dev_tools). Key features: three serialization modes (full, summary, single component by UUID); targeted CRUD operations on individual components without full round-trips; batch operations with atomic rollback; JSON schema generation per entity type/bundle; opaque-data protection so undeclared Layout Builder internals are preserved and never exposed to AI; a managed-keys and context/guidance system declared via YAML or hooks; on-demand skills; workspace enforcement; and an extensible tagged-service field-handler system. Access is enforced against the acting user throughout: every read, write, create, and field operation routes through a central fail-closed access checker, and nothing is ever saved implicitly — the caller decides whether to save, tempstore, or discard.
